scenes.headline: How a grep searches by meaning, not by string
scenes.sub: jev-semgrep asks a decision model about every line, and thresholds the answer.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Piccolo! jev-semgrep is a grep whose pattern is a sentence. Here's how it questions every line, and why that can do what vectors can't.

scenes.text: Don't compare vectors. Ask a decision model whether each line matches a proposition, and get a probability, which, unlike cosine distance, has a complement.
scenes.say: Don't compare vectors. Ask a decision model whether each line matches a proposition. You get a probability, and unlike cosine distance, a probability has a complement.

scenes.title: One request, thirty lines, many questions

steps.say: The file goes out thirty numbered lines at a time, as one shared state.
For every line and every meaning, a yes-or-no question: does line seven match this meaning? One request carries them all.

steps.note: each line is judged beside its neighbours in the chunk
steps.say: Jev returns a probability for each. Lines above the threshold are printed, and NOT is one minus the probability.

left.title: Vector search
items: Each line is embedded before any query exists
Cosine is distance, with no complement
A sentence and its negation land together
left.say: An embedding is computed before your query exists, and cosine is distance. A sentence and its negation land right next to each other.

right.title: A proposition per line
items: The model reads line and question together
NOT is one minus the probability
right.say: Jev reads the line and the question together, so AND, OR and NOT become plain operations on probabilities.

scenes.title: Where it goes in Next.js 16
scenes.say: The article then builds it into Next.js sixteen.

items.text: A Route Handler, not a Server Action
items.say: A route handler, because server actions run one at a time.

items.text: Cache the POST by its body
items.say: Cache each request by its body: the lines, the propositions, the pinned model.

items.text: Keep the threshold out of the key
items.say: Keep the threshold out of the key, so changing it costs nothing.
And stream verdicts as each chunk lands.

scenes.label: one pass over this site's 49,490 lines, for one meaning
scenes.note: no index, so every query pays for the corpus again
scenes.say: There's no index, so every query pays for the whole corpus again. One pass over this site is about eleven cents and eighty-three seconds.

scenes.text: Search by meaning works when the model reads the question with the line; the price is paying for every line, every query.
scenes.mark: reads the question with the line

recap: Thirty lines and many questions per request
A probability's complement makes NOT possible
No index: every query pays again
scenes.say: To recap: thirty lines per request, NOT from a probability's complement, and a bill paid on every query.
